recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future wording change beyond the applied resolution should be handled as a new Jira/THO terminology proposal rather than as a core source edit.
issue_request: FHIR-19772 was an OO Applied/Persuasive clarification asking to change the ReferenceRange meaning code `normal` from a strict two-standard-deviation definition to wording that describes expected values for a normal member of the relevant control population and treats the two-standard-deviation rule as typical.
initial_application: Commit f103fbd30441a7596bc298842427ef0fdf1be564 pre-applied GF#19772 by updating `source/observation/codesystem-referencerange-meaning.xml` to the resolved wording. The earlier strict wording had been introduced by GF#16139 in commit 1e59a65e1b6dc1798196f55d782d17e3400b1355.
additional_context: Commit 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 later removed the core CodeSystem source during the UTG/THO content move. Current core source keeps Observation and ObservationDefinition bound to `ValueSet/referencerange-meaning`, whose compose includes the external THO CodeSystem. Current THO JSON and the build/current published ValueSet pages show the accepted definition. FHIR-19773 from the same discussion was resolved no-change and was not decided here.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the authoritative code definition is no longer maintained in FHIR core source and the current core ValueSet/rendered expansion already contains the accepted FHIR-19772 wording.

related_jiras.note: Same Zulip/reference range thread asked to add a non-critical code, but Jira resolved it Not Persuasive/No Change and this reconciliation did not decide it.

evidence_items.summary: Applied/Persuasive OO issue requested a less restrictive definition for the ReferenceRange meaning code `normal`.
evidence_items.learned: This is the final Jira request and establishes the wording to verify in current source/output.

evidence_items.locator: #Orders and Observation WG > ReferenceRange value set - type/meaning
evidence_items.summary: The December 2018 thread identified the old definition as too strict and converged on the looser wording used by FHIR-19772.
evidence_items.learned: The thread supports the Jira resolution and shows why the two-standard-deviation text should be only typical guidance.

evidence_items.summary: Commit `healthedata1-preapply-GF#19772-make-normal-def-less-restrictive` changed the normal code definition in the then-core CodeSystem source.
evidence_items.learned: FHIR-19772 was historically applied before the CodeSystem moved out of core.

evidence_items.summary: Commit `Phase 1 removing UTG Content from core build` deleted `source/observation/codesystem-referencerange-meaning.xml` with the FHIR-19772 wording present.
evidence_items.learned: The authoritative code definition is no longer maintained as FHIR core source.

evidence_items.summary: Current active core source binds Observation.referenceRange.type to ValueSet/referencerange-meaning, whose compose includes THO CodeSystem/referencerange-meaning.
evidence_items.learned: Core source is in build scope and correctly delegates code definitions to the maintained external terminology source.
